nodes.label: First fall degree d_F (Nagao Def. 5)
nodes.statement: For f_1..f_M over F_2, a fall at degree d is a tuple (g_i) with max_i deg(g_i f_i) = d, deg(sum g_i f_i) < d and sum g_i f_i != 0; d_F is the least such d.
nodes.scope: Equality reading. The printed condition reads max_i deg(g_i f_i) >= d; the two readings agree on some systems and not others. The field equations may sit outside (F) or inside (F with S_fe) the generating set.

formal.notes: Mask encoding of F_2[X, Y] up to degree 7; equality reading only.

nodes.label: Fake first fall degree d'_F (Nagao Def. 6)
nodes.statement: d'_F is defined as d_F with every degree taken after reduction modulo the field equations S_fe = {X_j^2 + X_j} and with the reduced sum required to be nonzero.
nodes.scope: Computable in the multilinear quotient, which is why estimates bound it; on its own it says nothing about the unreduced solver trace.

nodes.label: Last fall degree
nodes.statement: The last fall degree of F is the least d such that every f in (F) lies in V_{F, max(d, deg f)}; equivalently (Caminata-Gorla Thm 2.8) the largest degree at which a degree fall occurs.
nodes.scope: Independent of term order and coordinates (Caminata-Gorla Remark 3.2).

nodes.label: Solving degree sd_sigma
nodes.statement: The least degree d such that Gaussian elimination on the degree-<=d Macaulay matrix under term order sigma yields a Groebner basis.
nodes.scope: Depends on sigma and on coordinates; this is the degree that sets F4/XL matrix size and therefore cost.

nodes.label: Nagao 2015/984 Lemma 4: d_F <= d'_F
nodes.statement: For every system over F_2, the first fall degree is at most the fake first fall degree.
nodes.scope: Refuted under the equality reading in both placements (witnesses A, B). Under the literal >= reading with the field equations inside, witness A gives True = Fake = 2, so the refutation is reading-specific; the paper declines to reproduce the proof of the lemma it derives Lemma 4 from.
failure_modes: A fake-degree certificate whose products have unreduced degree above d'_F does not certify a true fall at d'_F
An estimate written 'd'_F small, so by Lemma 4 d_F small' understates the degree
non_implications: Does not refute Nagao's Proposition 5, only the justification offered for it
Does not bear on Propositions 2 and 3, which exhibit explicit certificates
Says nothing about descended summation-polynomial systems at any n

nodes.label: Witnesses A, B: d'_F = 2 < d_F = 3 over F_2
nodes.statement: Witness A {X^2 Y, X Y + X} and witness B {X1 X2 + X3, X1 X3 + X2} have d'_F = 2 and d_F = 3 with the field equations outside and inside the generating set (equality reading).
nodes.scope: Exact finite computation. A: hand proof, three independent implementations, and a core-Lean decide +kernel check awaiting the proof gate. B and the census: native only.

formal.notes: Bridges argued, not proved in Lean: mask completeness for degree <= k, and reduction as a ring homomorphism.

nodes.label: Caminata-Gorla: sd = max(last fall, max GB degree)
nodes.statement: For a degree-compatible term order sigma, sd_sigma(F) = max{d_lastfall(F), maxGBdeg_sigma(F)} (Thm 3.1); equivalently sd_sigma(F) = max_i d_{g_i} over a reduced Groebner basis (Cor. 3.3).
nodes.scope: Rigorous. Fails for non-degree-compatible orders (Example 3.4). It is the sound bridge from a degree invariant to solver cost; a first fall degree is a lower-end quantity and is not in it.

nodes.label: Kosters-Yeo: descended S_3 has first fall degree 2
nodes.statement: For ordinary curves over F_2^n the Weil descent of the third summation polynomial generically has first fall degree 2, from a group morphism to F_2 that yields a linear polynomial; in their Magma runs the degree of regularity rises from 3 (n = 12) to >= 5 (n = 40) while the first fall degree stays 2.
nodes.scope: The first-fall value is a theorem (Cor. 4.11, Remark 4.12); the degree-of-regularity growth is their measurement on one random curve per n. Together they show the first fall degree does not track the solver degree on summation systems.

nodes.label: HKYY: n-independent last fall degree (zero-dim only)
nodes.statement: For zero-dimensional systems over F_{q^n}, the last fall degree of the Weil descent system is bounded independently of n.
nodes.scope: Zero-dimensional systems only; summation-polynomial descents with a factor-base subspace are not zero-dimensional, so this gives no bound for ECDLP relation search.

nodes.label: Nagao 2015/984: polynomial-time binary ECDLP under FFDA
nodes.statement: Nagao claims O(n^(8w+1)) for ECDLP over F_2^n (and O(n^((6p+2)w+1)) for p >= 3) using a disjoint factor base and a first-fall-degree bound (Proposition 5).
nodes.scope: Conditional twice: on the first-fall-degree assumption, and (for the justification offered) on Lemma 4, which is refuted under the equality reading. Not a usable cost.
assumptions: First fall degree controls the solving degree

cited_by.note: quotes the exponent, marks it suspect

nodes.label: ECC2K-130 IC projection 2^86 (FFDA)
nodes.statement: Petit-Quisquater / Kousidis-Wiemers degree formulas (D = m^2 + 1, D = m^2 - m + 1) give a projected index-calculus cost of 2^86.0 at n = 131 (2^69.0 at w = 9/4), against matched rho about 2^60.8.
nodes.scope: Conditional on the first-fall-degree assumption, which THM-KY-S3-FIRST-FALL-TWO and the repository's own ladders contradict for summation systems. Already labelled conditional at every use; listed so that any future row built on it inherits the taint.
assumptions: First fall degree controls the solving degree

nodes.label: Does Nagao Prop. 5 survive without Lemma 4?
nodes.statement: Decide whether Proposition 5 of Nagao 2015/984 holds by a route that avoids Lemma 4: either exhibit, per instance family, fake-degree certificates whose products already have unreduced degree <= d'_F (which recovers the true bound), or find a family where the true first fall degree exceeds the fake bound used.
nodes.scope: Blocked on a PDF-level transcription of Definitions 5, 6, Lemma 4 and Proposition 5.

nodes.label: Reverse inequality d'_F <= d_F (outside placement)?
nodes.statement: Prove or refute: with the field equations outside the generating set, d'_F <= d_F for every system over F_2 (equality reading).
nodes.scope: Candidate repair. The 7875-pair census (three variables, degree <= 2 multilinear pairs, cap 6) has d_F < d'_F in 0 pairs outside and 224 inside, so the inside form of the reverse inequality is already false; the outside form has no counterexample in that population only.

nodes.label: Every degree-based cost must pass through sd or last fall
nodes.statement: A cost row built from a degree must state which degree it uses; only a measured solving degree, or a proved bound on max{last fall degree, max GB degree} (Caminata-Gorla Thm 3.1), is a sound input. First fall, fake first fall and semi-regular degree-of-regularity values are lower-end or model quantities and leave the row conditional.
nodes.scope: Obligation on every node tagged first-fall-degree; open until each such estimate is either re-derived through the bridge or kept labelled conditional.
